decisions.decision: Apply Path A (5 surgical hardening edits via /gsd:plan-phase 56 --reviews) instead of Path B (execute-as-is + defer)
decisions.rationale: Codex MEDIUM concerns are operational hardening; ~20min replan cost is far less than re-debugging in CI later. Edits stay surgical — architecture and wave structure preserved.

decisions.decision: Skip Claude CLI in /gsd:review for cross-AI independence
decisions.rationale: Running inside Claude Code; reviewing with the same runtime collapses the value of cross-AI peer review. Gemini + Codex provided sufficient independence (different MEDIUM verdicts, different concerns surfaced).

decisions.decision: Stay line-by-line in extractClaims (vs Codex's whole-file scan suggestion)
decisions.rationale: Architectural simplicity wins; the multi-line risk is low (current docs all single-line per sanity test added in Edit 3). JSDoc constraint + sanity test provide an early-warning guardrail without re-architecting the regex extractor.

decisions.decision: Derive missingDocPolicy from --root presence + isRepoRoot helper, NOT a new CLI flag
decisions.rationale: Honors D-18 (4 CLI flags only). The runtime can infer fixture-mode vs production-mode from path semantics alone (look for package.json + .gitignore co-presence). New flag would add user-facing surface area for a behavior that's deterministic from existing inputs.

CONTEXT.md was decisions-locked but the concrete regex shapes for the 9 metrics across 3 living docs were NOT enumerated. Research produced (a) 14-drift-record ground truth Wave 3 needs, (b) Nyquist Dimension 8 Validation Architecture, (c) confirmation that line-by-line approach is safe. Skipping research would have left these as planning gaps.

decisions.decision: Ran Gemini and Codex reviewers in parallel (vs workflow's sequential default)
decisions.rationale: Different services, no shared rate limits. Workflow's caveat about rate limits applies to same-vendor sequencing; cross-vendor parallelism saves ~5min and has zero conflict risk.
